name: acct
description: The acct() system call enables or disables process accounting. If a filename is provided, it turns on accounting and appends records for each terminating process to the specified file. If NULL is passed, accounting is turned off.

parameters.name: filename
parameters.description: The name of an existing file to append accounting records to, or NULL to disable accounting.

return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set to indicate the error

errors.description: Write permission is denied for the specified file, or search permission is denied for one of the directories in the path prefix, or filename is not a regular file.
Filename points outside the accessible address space.
Error writing to the file filename.
Too many symbolic links were encountered in resolving filename.
The system-wide limit on the total number of open files has been reached.
The specified file does not exist.
BSD process accounting has not been enabled in the kernel.
A component used as a directory in filename is not a directory.
The calling process lacks the necessary privilege (requires CAP_SYS_PACCT on Linux).
Filename refers to a file on a read-only filesystem.
No more free file structures or out of memory.

bugs: No accounting is produced for programs running during a system crash, and nonterminating processes are never accounted for.
